units.title: Literary Works
units.intro: Grammar: a review of subordination (subordinate clauses) and lexical cohesion through collocation.

cards.title: Subordination
rule: A **subordinate clause** cannot stand alone; it depends on a main clause. It starts with a **subordinator**: time (*when, while, after, before, until*), reason (*because, since, as*), contrast (*although, though, whereas*), condition (*if, unless*), purpose (*so that*), relative (*who, which, that*).
Comma rule: when the subordinate clause comes **first**, use a comma: ***Although the novel is long,** it is exciting.*

examples.text: Because the story was sad, many readers cried.
Although he was poor. He was happy.
examples.fix: Although he was poor, he was happy.

examples.text: She read the poem until she understood it.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The manager rejected the proposal because he felt that ________ details were provided to support the budget.

steps.text: The blank modifies the noun 'details'. 'Details' is a plural countable noun (indicated by the '-s' ending).
Uncountable quantifiers like 'little' and 'a little' cannot modify plural countable nouns. 'Too few' is the correct quantifier for countable nouns in a negative context.
Tigrinya speakers often conflate 'few' and 'little' as both translate to 'ውሑድ' or 'ቅሩብ'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Although the construction project has been delayed, ________ progress has been made this week.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Progress' is an uncountable noun in English. It cannot be pluralized and cannot pair with countable quantifiers.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
'A few' and 'many' are strictly countable. 'Few' is also countable. 'Some' can modify both countable and uncountable nouns, making it the only grammatically viable option here.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The police ________ investigating the robbery that occurred near the national bank.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Police' is a collective noun that is grammatically plural and always takes a plural verb.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Because 'police' does not end in '-s', many non-native speakers mistake it for a singular noun and pair it with singular verbs like 'is' or 'was'. This is a highly targeted agreement trap in the ESSLCE.

**Step 3: Tigr

cards.title: Lexical cohesion: collocation
rule: **Collocations** are words that naturally go together: *make a decision, do homework, heavy rain, strong tea, take a photo, pay attention, commit a crime*. Using correct collocations makes writing natural and connects ideas.
Writers also link sentences by **repeating** key words and using **synonyms**.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **MAKE** creates something new (a decision, a plan); **DO** carries out a task (homework, the dishes).

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Subordinate clauses depend on a main clause and start with subordinators of time, reason, contrast, condition and purpose; use a comma when they come first. Collocations are natural word partners such as make a decision and do homework.
